objectives.text: Keep Nayib Bukele in the presidency past the old limits. On 31 July 2025 the Legislative Assembly, with the ruling New Ideas supermajority, approved constitutional changes allowing indefinite presidential re-election and six-year terms, and dropping the runoff (57 votes in favour, 3 against). The changes also propose ending the current term on 1 June 2027 rather than 2029.

grand_strategy.reading:
El Salvador's government rests on one proof of performance, the crackdown on the gangs under a state of emergency, and turns it into a claim to stay in office: the 2025 reform removes the term limit that the proof was meant to justify. Its links with the outside world are transactional and, in this card, rest on one arrangement with Washington for deportees. The weak point is the one the card cannot yet measure well: whether a state that depends on US migration cooperation can keep a crackdown that a prominent rights group now calls repression.

After the ambush of 18 October in Port-au-Prince, Bukele said on 21 October that the four Salvadoran personnel were held by the gangs and launched a rescue operation. About 100 special forces were sent to Haiti on 22 October (AP); a Reuters report of 27 October puts the total near 1,000 in staggered waves, with the command still unclear. The Haiti mission is the card's first military link outside the Washington arrangement, and the gangs that hold the men are the same kind of armed group the crackdown targets at home. Status unresolved in the sources read up to 27 October.

stances.note: Transactional, no treaty. The grade is our reading (confidence C): the sources name a deportation arrangement (the National Security Strategy, tier 1) and report Washington's shift from concern to quiet acceptance as Bukele moved toward re-election (AP, read in a search summary). Warming rests on the arrangement, not on a dated statement. Bond none: no shared identity and no open grievance found. The CECOT and remittance figures are not in the sources read.

stances.note: Our reading (confidence C), added 2026-10-29. Salvadoran personnel are in Haiti under the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force, to which El Salvador is one of several contributing countries; Haiti's government called the abduction an "absolute priority" (AP, 22 Oct). That is transactional cooperation without alignment, the partner reading; no treaty or bilateral security agreement was found in the sources read. Trend warming: the Salvadoran commitment grew in the days after the ambush, from about 100 special forces on 22 October to a reported 1,000 by 27 October (Reuters, one unnamed Haitian source, so the figure is the weakest part of this stance). Bond none: no kinship or grievance found. Command and duration of the contingent are unclear.

stances_toward.note: Added 29 October 2026 in the delta pass on the events of 18-21 October. El Salvador has personnel in the Gang Suppression Force: pilots and technical staff for medical evacuation, by the account of President Bukele (AP, 21 Oct). Four of them went missing after the gang ambush of 18 October in Croix-des-Bouquets; El Salvador announced a rescue operation on 21 October, and more special forces reached Haiti on 22 October (Tico Times, 25 Oct). Grade partner: a contributor to a UN-authorised force, with no treaty or alliance named in the sources, so this is our reading (confidence C). Trend warming: the Haitian government called the captives its foremost concern and said it was deploying all the assets needed (AP, 21 Oct). The since date is the first report of the Salvadoran contingent in the sources read, not the start of that deployment, which the sources do not date. Bond none: no shared identity or open wound is named.

stances_toward.note: Neutral with friction. In March 2025 Sheinbaum answered Bukele with a call for respect for Mexico (Mexico News Daily headline of 21 Mar 2025, body not read), and the question was whether Mexicans deported from the US could be sent to the CECOT prison in El Salvador (Mexico said no Mexican should go anywhere but Mexico; search summary). El Salvador and Honduras were the two governments that backed the 3 Jan 2026 US strikes on Venezuela while Mexico condemned them (Fox News). Neutral and not rival: no sanction, rupture or claim is recorded and trade or migration cooperation is not read; the friction is rhetorical and over third-country deportation. Bond none, our reading. Confidence C: headline and search summary only. Gap: Bukele's actual words, any 2026 bilateral contact, Salvadoran transit of Mexican deportees.
